message.content: Build the plumbing so real per-game LOGOS display across Nxeon (marketing + customer portal), replacing the generic 🎮 emoji/gradient placeholders. Work ONLY in `/opt/nxeon-wt-gamelogo` (branch feature/game-logos). Commit + push when done. Do NOT run npm build/prisma — write code + `npx tsc --noEmit`. ## Context - Canonical game slugs: `lib/games.ts` → `GAME_FAMILIES = ["minecraft","valheim","rust","palworld","cs2","terraria"]`. - Existing logo files (partial, inconsistent): `public/logos/minecraft.svg`, `public/logos/cs2.svg`, `public/logos/counterstrike.svg`, `public/logos/rust.png`, `public/logos/palworld.png`, `public/logos/valheim.png` (no terraria). - The OWNER is sourcing official logos and will drop them at **`public/logos/games/.svg`** (or .png) — that path is the PRIMARY source. Build for that convention. - Current render placeholders: `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx` has `GAME_META` with `glyph: "🎮"` emoji + `from`/`to` hex gradients (used ~L97 and ~L184). `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx` game sub-tabs render emoji. `components/marketing/GameLandingPage.tsx` (the per-game SEO pages) and `components/customer/GameDeploy.tsx` (customer game order flow) also show game identity. ## Build a shared `GameLogo` component `components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx` (or a shared location importable by both marketing + customer): props `{ family: GameFamily | string, size?, className? }`. Resolution order, gracefully falling back: 1. `public/logos/games/.svg` if present → render via next/image or . 2. else the existing `public/logos/.{svg,png}` (map cs2→cs2.svg, rust→rust.png, palworld→palworld.png, valheim→valheim.png, minecraft→minecraft.svg). 3. else the current emoji glyph from GAME_META as final fallback. Since we can't know at build time which files the owner has added, prefer a robust approach: render an `` that falls back to the known existing asset then the emoji — OR keep a small per-family asset map with the best currently-known path, and default new/missing ones to the `/logos/games/` path so the owner's drop-ins "just work". Pick whichever is clean and SSR-safe (a client component with onError fallback is fine; if you keep it a server component, use a static per-family path map with the emoji as the typed fallback). Keep the game's brand color (existing GAME_META from/to) available for a subtle glow/ring behind the logo so it still looks designed. ## Wire it in (replace emoji glyphs with ``) - `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx` — the game cards/sub-sections (both ~L97 and ~L184 usages) show `` instead of the emoji glyph, keeping the brand-color glow. - `components/marketing/GameLandingPage.tsx` — the per-game hero/identity uses ``. - `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx` — the game-family sub-tabs show the logo (small) instead of/alongside the emoji. - `components/customer/GameDeploy.tsx` — the game picker in the customer deploy flow shows ``. Keep all copy/prices/claims unchanged; DB-fed prices untouched; no VAT work; no amber except semantic. Respect the existing theme (navy/violet/cyan, Geist). ## Also - Create `public/logos/games/.gitkeep` (the dir exists) so the convention path is real, and add a short comment somewhere (e.g. atop GameLogo.tsx) documenting the drop-in convention + the six filenames. - If terraria has no asset anywhere, its GameLogo simply falls back to the emoji until the owner adds `public/logos/games/terraria.svg` — that's expected; don't fabricate a logo. ## Output `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (report it). Commit + push to origin/feature/game-logos. Report: the GameLogo resolution strategy, every surface you wired it into, and confirm copy/prices unchanged. This previews on staging; the owner will drop official logos into public/logos/games/ afterward.

Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. - anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
